summary: Reproduced the flat DeepSeek-V4 RoPE kernel reading and writing padded columns when rope_dim is not a power of two, then fixed it by passing the real width as a constexpr, clamping padded-lane load addresses, and masking padded-lane stores. Power-of-two kernels retain their direct addressing path.

tests.what_was_measured: Before the source fix: 5 failed and 10 passed. The independent PyTorch reference detected wrong values for non-power-of-two widths, and sentinel-backed views detected 16, 256, and 512 overwritten elements past rope_dim for widths 6, 96, and 192. Power-of-two controls 64 and 128 passed. Raw output: reports/j-5d714fda3516/raw/pytest-before.log

After the source fix: all 15 GPU regression and boundary cases passed against an independent PyTorch complex-rotation reference and sentinel-backed storage. Raw output: reports/j-5d714fda3516/raw/pytest-after.log
The patch contains no whitespace errors.

Formatting tools were attempted but are not installed in the prepared interpreter (No module named ruff/black). Raw output: reports/j-5d714fda3516/raw/ruff.log and reports/j-5d714fda3516/raw/black.log

gpu_execution.evidence: All focused tests executed Triton kernels on the single assigned AMD Instinct MI350X, gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-, using torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 and HIP 7.2.26015. Raw environment output: reports/j-5d714fda3516/raw/environment.log

remaining_limitations: Validation used the assigned AMD gfx950 GPU, not the NVIDIA B200 environment from the original report; CUDA compute-sanitizer evidence was therefore not reproduced.

No full model or distributed workload was run. The affected path is an opt-in kernel path and current DeepSeek-V4 uses a power-of-two rotary width; focused kernel execution is the relevant reproduction.
The prepared interpreter does not include ruff or black, so those checks could not run; git diff --check passed.
